Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models

paper.arxiv.2307.15043

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2307.15043v2. Universal multi-prompt optimization and disclosed historical attack conditions establish red-team/evaluation scope. Source table/prose discrepancies remain; no current vulnerability claim or operational attack instructions added. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Transfer results depend on historical model versions, sampling and interface conditions; the authors discuss shared training/distillation as a potential transfer confound and disclosed findings before publication.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Across 388 harmful behaviors, Table 2 reports ensemble transfer attack success rates of 86.6% for GPT-3.5 and 46.9% for GPT-4, compared with 1.8% and 8.0% for the behavior-only baseline; ensemble success means at least one suffix succeeds.
